transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-20
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Veridian ML), Tom (Veridian Infra), Priya (Veridian Security), Daniel (Veridian PM)

Summary:
Short sit-down to align on POC success criteria, what scripts the customer will send, how we marshal their client harness, and to decide on streaming vs non-streaming workload shape for the first benchmark run. Also covered telemetry contract and KMS questions.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency p95, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy drop tolerance)
- Script marshalling: input shape, multi-turn state, conversation context size
- Harness adapter: streaming integration, ok-to-fallthrough behaviors, backpressure
- Telemetry fields and audit log needs for security/compliance
- Timeline and next steps for sample upload and test windows

Action items (captured above in metadata).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Sofia: Hey, Sofia here. I'm the Head of ML at Veridian.
[00:08] Tom: Tom, infra.
[00:09] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:11] Daniel: Daniel, product.
[00:12] Liam: Liam from Redwood, SE.
[00:14] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to get to a concrete benchmark playbook and agree on what scripts you'll hand us and what acceptance looks like, yes?
[00:22] Sofia: Yep. Also want to make sure we don't bias the tests towards your hosted sweet spot, like we care about the private deployment profile too since it's compliance-heavy.
[00:31] Maya: Totally. We'll define both hosted and private runs. We'll note differences in networking warmup and KV-cache warmup expectations.
[00:38] Tom: Quick clarifying Q from infra: our calls are usually multi-turn assistant workflows, about 4-6 turns average, tokens per request around 350, but with a tail of long contexts for specialist support cases up to 4k tokens.
[00:51] Liam: Ok that's useful. For the harness, we need the typical token histogram and an example of the long-context case. Also, is streaming required? Can you tolerate non-streaming for the long-context runs?
[01:04] Sofia: For interactive product paths, streaming matters to UX. For batch analytics flows we can do non-streaming. For the POC let's prioritize streaming for the interactive slice and run a non-streaming long-context slice separately.
[01:19] Daniel: We're primarily evaluating: 1) p95 latency under interactive load, target p95 < 300ms for 350-token responses; 2) sustained throughput for background batch jobs measured as tokens/sec; 3) accuracy/regression within 2% of our baseline model.
[01:35] Maya: Good concrete targets. We'll translate that into run parameters: interactive slice with target RPS 50, avg response 350 tokens, streaming enabled. Background batch slice with concurrency 8, non-streaming, avg response 1200 tokens.
[01:50] Tom: Where did 50 RPS come from? Our peak for a single microservice is closer to 200 RPS but we want to phase it. For POC start lower to validate correctness.
[02:01] Maya: We can run a ramp: smoke at 20 RPS, steady-state at 100 RPS, peak at 200 RPS for a short soak. We'll include cold-start behavior too.
[02:13] Sofia: Important: KV cache warmup is critical—our baseline has warm KV cache for common prefixes. We need to see both cold and warm runs.
[02:23] Liam: We'll model a warm-up window—preload common keys as part of the harness, and note warm vs cold performance in the report. We'll instrument cache hit ratios.
[02:33] Priya: Security side: we need to see audit logs with user- and request-level correlation ID, and KMS key policies. Are you able to stream logs to our S3?
[02:43] Liam: Yes, we can stream telemetry. For Private we'll support pulling audit logs to customer-managed S3 and Kinesis. For Hosted we'll provide an export mechanism. We'll include correlation_id, model_version, node_id, and token_count in telemetry.
[02:58] Priya: Token_count is non-negotiable for chargeback. Also need cryptographic envelope headers for the KMS flows.
[03:06] Maya: Noted. We'll include a KMS integration diagram in the artifacts.
[03:09] Daniel: Can you add in the playbook what constitutes a pass/fail for the accuracy/regression? We run a small eval set, do you support per-prompt scoring?
[03:19] Liam: Yes, the harness supports per-prompt scoring and aggregate thresholds. We can ingest your eval CSV with prompts and reference answers. We'll produce a delta against your baseline.
[03:28] Sofia: Good. For the harness adapter — what's the expected format for our scripts? We have Python-based client scripts that do some pre-tokenization and then call a local proxy before hitting your endpoint.
[03:39] Maya: Best is to provide the canonical script and an API shim spec. We will build a minimal adapter that calls your shim. The adapter should be idempotent and support retries/backoff.
[03:49] Tom: Our current shim supports both streaming and non-streaming via a flag, but it uses grpc for streaming and HTTP for batch. Would Redwood's harness handle grpc streams?
[03:58] Liam: Our harness can support HTTP streaming and gRPC streaming; the adapter will need to translate into the harness' internal stream contract. We'll include an example gRPC-to-harness adapter.
[04:10] Daniel: How do you handle pacing/backpressure? Live product traffic has bursts and we can't drop user sessions.
[04:17] Liam: Two things: continuous batching inside the runtime and per-request prioritization. The harness will simulate bursts using Poisson and sawtooth load shapes. We can configure graceful degradation policies — for example, fall back to a cheaper model variant under overload.
[04:33] Sofia: We do want to see the fall-through case in the POC. Show us the quality delta when the system switches to a smaller quantized model. That’s a sales concern too.
[04:43] Maya: We'll include a model-fallback run and a small eval to measure quality drop.
[04:46] Priya: Another security requirement — data residency. Some logs must stay in our EU account. For Private deployment will everything stay in our VPC?
[04:57] Liam: For Private, yes. The control plane may still be managed, but all inference nodes and logs can be in your VPC. We'll provide an on-prem tarball if you want air-gapped install.
[05:09] Tom: Cost measurement: how granular are your cost metrics? We want per-route token cost and per-request latency breakdown.
[05:17] Maya: Console will show per-route token counts, per-model cost per token, and node-level latency breakdowns (scheduling, kernel, network). For the POC we'll provide a CSV breakdown.
[05:27] Daniel: I have a question about long-context runs: the developer says sometimes the input includes large attachments base64-encoded which spikes tokens. How do we avoid these skewing median numbers?
[05:37] Liam: The playbook will suggest outlier filtering: discard top 1% for summary metrics but report tail statistics separately. We'll also run a dedicated 'attachment' slice showing worst-case numbers.
[05:48] Sofia: For the harness we need to map our session affinity: same user multiple requests to preserve KV cache behaviors. Can the harness emulate sticky sessions?
[05:58] Liam: Yes. We'll support user-id affinity and KV warm paths. We'll need your session mapping rules.
[06:04] Priya: About telemetry again — do you redaction on PII? We can't send unredacted user data to a hosted environment.
[06:12] Maya: We recommend local redaction pre-harness. For Private you can keep full logs. For Hosted we offer configurable redaction rules and field-level hashing.
[06:23] Tom: Timeline check — what's realistic for a two-week POC? We need time to adapt scripts and security review.
[06:29] Maya: Two-week POC is tight but doable if you can turn around scripts quickly. Proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) share scripts and histograms; week 1 we wire harness adapter and do smoke tests; week 2 run full benchmark and produce report. If security review delays, we can scope a one-week soft run first.
[06:48] Sofia: We can commit to sending scripts by Monday. Security will need artifacts by mid-week.
[06:54] Priya: I'll need the SOC2 packet and KMS diagram before we move scripts to hosted. Can Maya send links?
[07:01] Maya: Yes, I'll send SOC2 and KMS diagram along with the playbook deck.
[07:06] Daniel: On acceptance criteria — confirm again: p95 <300ms for streaming interactive (350 tokens) and no more than 2% regression in accuracy?
[07:14] Liam: Yes, and also sustained tokens/sec for batch slice > X — we need a target from you.
[07:19] Daniel: For batch we'd like at least 15k tokens/sec sustained in the small dedicated pool equivalent.
[07:25] Maya: We'll map that to a dedicated pool config and give pricing bands.
[07:29] Sofia: A minor note: our baseline model uses 8-bit quantization on certain layers, so we'd like Redwood's quant profiles documented in the playbook.
[07:39] Liam: We'll include recommended quantization profiles and note known incompatibilities.
[07:44] (small cross talk)
[07:48] Tom: For the harness adapter, can you accept a zip containing a virtualenv plus scripts, or do you want only code snippets?
[07:55] Liam: A zip with a simple install script is fine. We'll run it in an isolated harness runner; avoid heavy native deps. If you have native libs we can containerize but that adds setup time.
[08:06] Priya: Any examples of audit fields you always include?
[08:09] Liam: correlation_id, request_ts, model_version, node_id, token_count, user_id_hash, tenant_id. We'll add encrypted_request_hash for traceability without exposing content.
[08:22] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps now.
[08:25] Maya: Action items: Liam will draft adapter checklist and gRPC example; Sofia will send scripts and histograms; Priya will review security artifacts; Maya will send playbook deck and SOC2; and we'll schedule the preliminary run for the week of 2027-01-31.
[08:44] Sofia: Sounds good. Also we'll note competitor benchmarking — we might ask to run a single sample against Bedrock to compare latency; that may be optional.
[08:53] Maya: We can do that but need explicit confirmation and keys.
[08:58] Daniel: Ok thanks everyone, good sync.
[09:02] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with the deck and links.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Customer emphasized streaming for interactive slice and explicit warm/cold KV cache runs.
- Security requires KMS diagram + SOC2 before hosted data handoff.
- Customer will provide samples and histograms; Redwood to provide harness adapter checklist and example gRPC shim.
- Acceptance criteria agreed: p95 latency target <300ms for 350-token streaming interactive; accuracy regression threshold 2%; batch sustained tokens/sec target 15k.

References mentioned:
- Playbook deck (to be shared)
- Example harness adapter repo (to be shared)
- SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration diagram (to be shared)

End of transcript.
